attribute_values.details: Hydroxyurea, hydroxycarbamide. HU in- hibits the ribonucleotide reductase and depletes cellular deoxy- nucleotide pools, thereby inducing replication stress and DNA damage.

attribute_values.name: 5-Fluorouracil
attribute_values.details: 5-FU is a pyrimidine analog that causes DNA and RNA stress by the incorporation of its derived metabo- lites into DNA and RNA and by the inhibition of thymidylate synthase, inducing deoxyribonucleotide pool imbalance.

attribute_values.name: Etoposide
attribute_values.details: Etoposide stabilizes the complex between DNA and topoisomerase II,48 leading to the induction of DNA double- strand breaks.

attribute_values.name: Rotenone
attribute_values.details: Rotenone inhibits the transfer of electrons from iron-sulfur centers in complex I to ubiquinone. Complex I is unable to pass off its electron to CoQ, creating a back-up of electrons within the mitochondrial matrix.

attribute_values.name: CCCP
attribute_values.details: Carbonyl cyanide m-chlorophenyl hydrazone. CCCP causes an uncoupling of the proton gradient that is established during the normal activity of electron carriers in the electron transport chain. CCCP acts essentially as an ionophore and reduces the ability of ATP synthase to function optimally.

attribute_values.name: FCCP
attribute_values.details: Carbonyl cyanide-p-trifluoromethoxyphenylhydrazone (FCCP) is an ionophore that is a mobile ion carrier. It is referred to as an uncoupling agent because it disrupts ATPsynthesis by transporting hydrogen ions through the mitochondrial membrane before they can be used to provide the energy for oxidative phosphorylation

attribute_values.name: Doxorubicin
attribute_values.details: Doxorubicin is a type of chemotherapy drug called an anthracycline. It slows or stops the growth of cancer cells by blocking an enzyme called topo isomerase 2.

attribute_values.name: Doxycycline
attribute_values.details: Doxycycline is a broad-spectrum antibiotic of the tetracycline class used in the treatment of infections caused by bacteria and certain parasites.

attribute_values.name: Etoposide
attribute_values.details: Etoposide is a medication used in the management and treatment of various cancers such as testicular, prostate, bladder, stomach, and lung cancer. It is in the topoisomerase II inhibitor class of medications.

attribute_values.name: CRISPR-mediated
attribute_values.details: A CRISPR-associated (Cas) enzyme is used to cleave target DNA, resulting in a double-strand break (DSB). The Cas enzyme is directed by the guide RNA (gRNA) to a user-defined site in the genome, and then the Cas enzyme cuts the DNA.

attribute_values.name: CRSPR+HDR mediated
attribute_values.details: HDR is an acronym for homology-directed repair, one of the common mechanisms for DNA double-strand break repair in eukaryotes. HDR can be used as part of CRISPR-mediated editing to introduce an exogenous DNA repair template composed of homology arms flanking a sequence of interest.

attribute_values.name: BiggyBac transposon
attribute_values.details: The PiggyBac (PB) transposon is a mobile genetic element that efficiently transposes between vectors and chromosomes via a 'cut and paste' mechanism. During transposition, the PB transposase recognizes transposon-specific inverted terminal repeat sequences (ITRs) located on both ends of the transposon vector and efficiently moves the contents from the original sites and integrates them into TTAA chromosomal sites

attribute_values.name: TALE nucleases
attribute_values.details: Transcription activator-like effector nucleases (TALEN) are restriction enzymes that can be engineered to cut specific sequences of DNA. They are made by fusing a TAL effector DNA-binding domain to a DNA cleavage domain (a nuclease which cuts DNA strands). Transcription activator-like effectors (TALEs) can be engineered to bind to practically any desired DNA sequence, so when combined with a nuclease, DNA can be cut at specific locations.

attribute_values.name: Zinc-finger nucleases
attribute_values.details: Zinc-finger nucleases (ZFNs) are artificial restriction enzymes generated by fusing a zinc finger DNA-binding domain to a DNA-cleavage domain. Zinc finger domains can be engineered to target specific desired DNA sequences and this enables zinc-finger nucleases to target unique sequences within complex genomes.

DSP contains an amine-reactive NHS ester at each end of an 8-carbon spacer arm.

attribute_values.name: DTBP
attribute_values.details: DTBP is dimethyl 3,3'-dithiobispropionimidate, a crosslinker that contains amine-reactive imidoester groups around an 8-atom spacer arm, whose central disulfide bond can be cleaved with reducing agents.

attribute_values.name: DTME
attribute_values.details: DTME (dithiobismaleimidoethane) is a mid-length, maleimide crosslinker for reversible covalent conjugation between sulfhydryl groups (e.g., protein or peptide cysteines) by reduction of the disulfide bond in the center of the spacer arm.

attribute_values.name: DTSSP
attribute_values.details: DTSSP (3,3'-dithiobis(sulfosuccinimidyl propionate))  is a popular water-soluble crosslinker that contains amine-reactive NHS-ester ends around an 8-atom spacer arm, whose central disulfide bond can be cleaved with reducing agents.

attribute_values.name: LC-SPDP

attribute_values.name: PDPH

attribute_values.name: PEG12-SPDP

attribute_values.name: PEG4-SPDP
attribute_values.details: PEG4-SPDP is a multifunctional crosslinker for protein conjugation via amine-to-amine or amine-to-sulfhydryl crosslinks that contain a 4-unit polyethylene glycol (PEG) group and a reducible (cleavable) disulfide bond.

attribute_values.name: SDAD

attribute_values.name: SMCC

attribute_values.name: SMPT

attribute_values.name: DSBU
attribute_values.details: Disuccinimidyl Dibutyric Urea (DSBU, BuUrBUU). Water-insoluble (dissolve first in DMF or DMSO). MS-cleavable and membrane-semi-permeable crosslinkers that contain an amine-reactive N-hydroxysuccinimide (NHS) ester at each end of a 11-atom spacer arm (DSBU). Contains a cleavable functionality in the linker region that enables cleavage in the gas phase using collision-induced dissociation (CID) during tandem MS (MS/MS) fragmentation. The MS cleavage of DSSO or DSBU generates diagnostic ion doublets during MS2, which distinguishes identification of cross-linked peptides from dead-end modifications.
